data.body:
Root cause PROVEN (Phase 1) — the fault is on the SENT side, not the model's indices.

MECHANISM. With ZERO Pass-1 findings the Pass-2 verify step still makes its single aggregate call: workflow_ops.plan_review_verify_inputs builds instructions as [verify_instructions(c) for c in (chunks or [[]])], so an empty finding list yields ONE empty chunk. review_kernel/verify.py verify_instructions() returned, for an empty batch, 'Verify each finding below by its index. Emit one verification per finding.' — an imperative to emit verifications with no finding listed. The verifier answers with indices 0..N-1; decide_ops.py:193 reshapes against valid_indices=range(len(findings)) = range(0), so every returned index is 'unexpected' (verify.py:236), the map is empty, and decide_ops.py:196-201 logs ERROR + records the violation into signed verdict coverage.

INDEX-BASIS FACT that pins the side: 0 is a member of range(n) for every n>=1, so index 0 appearing in 'unexpected' can ONLY mean len(findings)==0 at decide. It is not a chunk-local vs global numbering error.

EVIDENCE (AC1) — captured request/response pair plus a census of 3908 stored REVIEW_RESULT events on the tickets branch:
* SENT side, captured: for findings=[] the request body is exactly 'Verify each finding below by its index. Emit one verification per finding.' and the index domain sent is []. No indices are offered.
* RETURNED side, captured live: coverage.verification_contract_violations = [{'unexpected': [0,1,2,3]}] on ticket 0c49; 43 such runs in total, unexpected sets always contiguous from 0, sizes 1..15, the single index [0] dominating.
* Cross-tab over the 3719 runs with llm_ran=true: (violation, has LLM findings) = (False,False) 898, (False,True) 2778, (True,False) 43, (True,True) ZERO. Perfect separation. 2778 healthy runs prove the index basis is correct whenever Pass-1 produces findings, so NO findings are being lost; violations occur only on the zero-finding path.

RULED OUT. (a) chunk-local vs global index basis — refuted by the 0-in-range arithmetic and by 2778 clean multi-finding runs; (b) findings dropped between verify and decide — refuted by the same cross-tab and by all 43 violation runs being PASS with zero LLM findings in every bucket; (c) a re-chunk between request and response — verify_request_chunks returns [] for an empty list, one empty chunk is synthesised, one request is sent (metrics.verify_requests=1); (d) model fault as primary — the model was handed a request that cannot be satisfied truthfully.

AC4 — can an INDETERMINATE finding BLOCK? For the Pass-2 path: NO. pass3_decide(None) returns decision='indeterminate', priority 0.0 (decide.py:542-551), short-circuiting BEFORE the blocking_enabled/block_threshold test, so blocking_enabled and the threshold are irrelevant to a degraded finding. partition_findings routes decision=='indeterminate' to parts['indeterminate'], never to blocking (orchestrator.py:339-346, with an assert that no block leaks into advisory). finalize_verdict blocks only on a non-empty blocking bucket (orchestrator.py:410). A degraded finding therefore can never cause BLOCK. It can flip PASS to INDETERMINATE, but ONLY via orchestrator.py:435 'elif indeterminate and not surfaced' — i.e. only when there is no surfaced advisory at all. If any advisory surfaces, degraded findings are absorbed silently and the verdict is PASS. So the Pass-2 failure mode is a silently UNVERIFIED finding that passes, not a spurious block. The separate coverage.verify_failed path (set only by workflow/plan_review_recovery.py:280) is the one that is fail-closed on blocking-enabled criteria (orchestrator.py:426); the reshape path never sets it.

The PREREQUISITE-COVERAGE indeterminate path is DIFFERENT and must not be conflated: decide_ops.py:312-339 sets coverage.prerequisite_indeterminate and actively RECLASSIFIES every non-DET blocking finding into indeterminate, and orchestrator.py:415 makes the verdict INDETERMINATE unconditionally. That path can remove real blocks; the Pass-2 path cannot create them.

BLAST RADIUS. None of the 43 affected runs lost a finding — all had zero LLM findings and a correct PASS. No previously-signed review needs revisiting on these grounds. The real costs were a wasted billable verify call per clean review, an alarming ERROR log, and a spurious verification_contract_violations record inside signed attestation coverage.

FIX (Phase 2, commit 0ab4a5b273c on fix/d5c7-pass2-indices). verify_instructions() now returns EMPTY_BATCH_INSTRUCTIONS = 'No findings to verify; return an empty verifications array.' for an empty batch, mirroring the contract prerequisite_workflow_ops.py already states for its own empty case. The shared kernel seam also fixes the identical empty case in code_review_verify_inputs (code_review/workflow_ops.py:274), so the sibling needs no separate edit.

RED-first: tests/unit/test_verify_empty_batch_contract.py failed at both the kernel seam and the live producer before the fix, passes after, and returns to RED when the old string is re-introduced. tests/unit/test_review_kernel.py's assertion that the empty batch says 'Emit one verification per finding' encoded the defect and was updated to the new contract.

Gates: pytest (not integration and not external) exit 0 (8879 passed, 31 skipped); make lint exit 0; make typecheck exit 0.

AC3 NOT DONE: a live review-plan run confirming no violation is outstanding. It needs a real billable run that also writes a REVIEW_RESULT event to the shared tickets branch, so it was left for the operator.
